newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News worried about Fairfax deal.
newsitem.headline: News worried about Fairfax deal.

text.p: Retiring News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley said on Wednesday that he is worried ministers in the national government had made a commitment to change cross-media rules that would allow billionaire Kerry Packer to buy publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.
"I'm concerned that there has been commitments or a commitment to get the cross media (changes) done by some ministers," Cowley told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"I don't think it's the Prime Minister (John Howard), but I'm worried there has been some commitment to get it done and put foreign ownership aside," Cowley said.
"What you would finish up with is allowing the Packer organisation to become a rather awesome media power in Australia," he said.
The government is reviewing cross-media rules set up by the former Labor government which stop television station owners from controlling major newspapers in the same city and vice-versa.

These rules prevent Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which owns the top-rating Nine television network, from buying more than 15 percent of Fairfax. Packer's son James Packer has said the company has Fairfax in its sights.
The government has also said it did not want to allow higher foreign ownership of media in Australia, which effectively would cap News' hefty newspaper and television interests here.
News is classified as a foreign company because Rupert Murdoch is a U.S. citizen despite being Australian-born.
Cowley, widely seen as Murdoch's right-hand man in Australia, said the cross media rules should be changed, but that foreign ownership rules should also be relaxed.

"There should be no government interference with the media, so the cross media laws should go, and so should all the other barriers including foreign ownership and we've got to be sure that we don't change the rules that allows an imbalance of ownership in the media," he said.
News Ltd publishes newspapers in most capital cities and accounts for about 70 percent of metropolitan newspaper circulation.
The key Fairfax publications are The Sydney Morning Herald, The (Melbourne) Age, and the Australian Financial Review national business daily. It also publishes magazines.
Seven Network Ltd chairman Kerry Stokes has also accused the government of having done a deal to deliver Fairfax to Packer. He later withdrew this comment.
Some commentators have said Packer's support for the government in the 1996 election is a factor in the government's support for changes to the cross-media rules.
Packer's 15 percent stake in Fairfax is only second to that of Brierley Investments Ltd of New Zealand which has 20 percent. Brierley has also said it would like to have a larger stake.
